Chapter 8: The Emotional Side of Quitting and Sticking.
When it comes to deciding whether to quit or keep going, let’s be honest—logic isn’t the only thing at play. Our emotions are right there in the driver’s seat. Fear, pride, hope, even guilt—they all have a way of clouding our judgment, sometimes making it tough to see the path ahead.
So, why do these feelings matter so much? Well, fear often shows up as that nagging anxiety—worrying about missing out, or being labeled a failure. Pride? It can keep us clinging to something that just isn’t working, simply because we don’t want to admit we were wrong. And hope... hope’s a double-edged sword. It can push us to keep going, but it can also blind us to reality. Then there’s guilt—the weight that comes from thinking we’re letting others down if we walk away.
Managing these emotions is key. Here are a few gentle ways you can navigate those tricky feelings:
First, try naming your emotions. Just saying to yourself, “Hey, I’m feeling scared,” or “I’m frustrated right now,” can actually take away some of their power.
Next, ask yourself—are you just uncomfortable because things are tough, or is this a sign that something truly isn’t right for you in the long run? That little bit of self-reflection can go a long way.
Don’t forget about self-compassion. Remind yourself: quitting when something isn’t working doesn’t mean you failed. Sometimes, it’s the wisest thing you can do.
And here’s a helpful trick—visualize both futures. Picture yourself sticking it out, and then imagine quitting. Which path feels more true to who you are and where you want to go?
Think about someone working a job they’ve outgrown. The fear of starting over and the pride from years of hard work can make leaving feel almost impossible. But by gently examining those emotions, it becomes clearer—are you just facing a temporary challenge, or is it time to move on?
Remember, emotional clarity isn’t about shutting off your feelings. It’s about understanding them well enough to make choices that really fit your bigger goals. In the end, whether you quit or stick, let it be an act of self-awareness—and courage.
